We have a LOT of characters to choose from. I would like to know everyone's go to character and why that is, and a reasoning behind it. Whether it's a personal reason (e.g. "I like Hal Jordan because I feel like I want to embody his constant unwavering willpower" ) or it's another reason ( e.g. "Dude. Just look at the raw power behind Etrigan"). It doesn't matter. I'm genuinely curious as to your favorite DC character (It doesn't have to be a hero either, it could be a villain, side character, or antihero.)
Favorite DC Character and why: go!

I know that it's really common, but I have to go with Batman. He's the whole reason I picked up comics in the first place, and his rogue gallery is by FAR the best. He character goes so deep, and over the years the Batman mythos has become one of the most in depth (aside from Green Lantern's, I think). Just overall, I think DC hit the nail on the head with Batman, Bob Kane and Bill Finger started something for the ages!

Batman (and Zorro) were also my first introductions to the Superhero world. Batman the Animated Series came out when I was 2 (92). So some of my earliest memories were sitting on my parent's bed and watching Batman with my older brother after he came home from school on the tiny little TV. When superman came out in '96, we'd watch that too. I was all about Batman, he was all about Superman.

I definitely credit Batman for introducing me to my favorite, Green Arrow (not that it was obvious or anything). Without Batman TAS, there'd be no Justice league series. I was about 14 when I got into the Comics. In high school and college, my collection really took off. Most of what I own is Green Arrow, Green Lantern, Catwoman, and recently Aquaman's new 52 line. See, my best friend is a lot like Hal Jordan. I'm a lot like Ollie Queen. So it was always a past time with us to send each other a gift of something both Green Lantern and Green Arrow, always together for christmas. One time I flew over for Christmas and we made Gingerbread Green Lantern and Green Arrow. Super fun stuff.

I like Ollie. I like how he makes mistakes and struggles to make them right. I like his political philosophies, and how if a system is broken, you fix it. I love the cheesiness of his lines, the strange surroundings that led to him having a life altering viewpoint, and the witty banter between Him, Barry, and Hal.

Also the boxing glove arrow.

I'm a Superman guy myself, but the whole Batman universe is very compelling, not that he can't function on his own. Robin/Nightwing, Alfred, Catwoman, Joker, Penguin, Batgirl, etc etc etc. They're all good characters and the relationships allow for some pretty complex storytelling.
Either Red Hood of Green Arrow. They are just bad ass characters.
Yeah. Red hood has definitely been an interesting addition to the stories!
Finishing off Red Hood and the Outlaws. Looking forward to starting Red Hood and Arsenal.
Awesome sauce! I'm still piecing together the New 52 lines, myself!

Red hood is one of my favorites too. The sad truth though is I have yet to get the story I want for him.

Jason Todd interests me a lot more as the damaged vigilante trying to find his place in the world and his relationship with the bat family than he does as an adventuring playboy like he is with the outlaws.

I have to go with Superman for nostalgia. I grew up watch Superman 2 on betamax, and then in high school the animated series by Paul Dini and Bruce Timm. I love that despite all of his strength, he still ends up using his brain to solve most of his problems. He also tries exceptional hard to do the right thing, not just for people but all life forms.

I have one. I've never experienced the problems I read about online. I have the 5 inch barrel extension kit as well as the factory barrel. The one I have doesn't seem to be that picky with ammo.
Well you feel free to box that up and mail it to me. :P

Mine has the problems; it manifests itself rarely on cheap ammo and about 25% of the time on subsonic.

Then again, I'm shooting subsonic in a gun with a reputation for being picky about ammo. What do I expect ;)

I've had one for a while now. It's picky, sure...but not super picky. It's accurate, light, and inexpensive. It's a nice first pistol IMO. I'm biased; it IS my first pistol. Disassembly isn't hard. Mags are always 10Rd, though.

It will happily work with CCI and other higher velocity rounds. Cheaper brands...it will choke a bit. I have some Federal? ammo that's really greasy and that seems to help things along, but not always.

The problem is a really stiff recoil spring. The manifestation of ammunition the firearm doesn't "like" is an FTE, sometimes FTE+FTF. If you're lucky you can get a stovepipe (for values of 'lucky'), but most of the time it'll just be a full FTE. Frankly if you're looking for something that'll force you to do Tap, Rack, Bang...stick some subsonic in it. You'll be doing TRB about 25% of the time, which will keep you on your toes. That 25% is streaky - you won't always be doing 2-3 taps; you'll sometimes do 5 per mag and sometimes you'll be like "holy crap, I got through the entire mag of this cheap ammo and didn't have an FTE once."

The Walther P22 also acts a lot like the PPK and similar firearms, so you won't have to retrain too much on those. My friends who have airsoft replicas of the PPK were able to work the P22 in seconds after seeing it. (I'm one of the few with firearms in my friendgroups)

Honestly I might recommend a Ruger Mk II or Mk III instead if you want a 100% reliable 22LR pistol that eats anything - but honestly, .22LR means the P22 is a target pistol (it even has a longer target barrel option) and it's great for that.

Remember, the problem is completely mitigatable with good ammo.

I decided on the Thermaltake v1 mini tower because of who many great reviews it has. It also seems to have some of the better heat management of the mini ITX cases.

I picked the GA-z97n-wifi for its compatibility with OCing the 4690k and its inbuilt wifi so we don't need an additional card. This will ensure where ever he might take his little pc he can join a network.
